title: Panning in acre-gui draws the whole scene again on every frame
body:
`View::show` in `crates/acre-gui/src/view.rs` draws the scene again whenever the zoom, the offset or the pane's size changes. A drag changes the offset on every frame. So each frame of a pan builds every primitive, sets every label's glyphs as paths, rasterizes the whole pane in software through `render::draw_view`, and uploads the texture. Jack finds panning laggy on the PrefixEncoder figure in the debug build. The release build does the same work per frame, more quickly.

## Proposal

- While the person drags, paint the last texture shifted by the drag, and draw the scene again when the drag stops.
- Draw a margin around the pane, so a short pan shows drawn content and not an empty edge.
- While zooming with the wheel, stretch the last texture and draw a sharp one once the wheel stops.

## Open

- Whether to cache glyph paths in `render`, so each full redraw costs less as well.
close_reason: View::texture_rect moves and scales the last texture during a pan or zoom, and View::draw runs again 150 ms after motion stops. Jack tried it in the release build and found it snappy. Glyph path caching was left out, since a full redraw no longer happens during a pan.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text: Implemented in crates/acre-gui/src/view.rs, not yet committed. The texture reaches a quarter of the pane past each edge (OVERDRAW). During a pan or zoom, View::texture_rect moves and scales the last texture, and View::draw runs again only 150 ms after the last motion (SETTLE), or at once when the texture no longer covers the pane. Glyph path caching in render is not done. Waiting on Jack to try panning in the release build.
